title: Counting Chargeable Days on Rate Lock Commitment Extensions for Clear-to-Close Files
content:
Clear-to-close files and **Rate Lock Commitment** extensions. The days of an extension that count toward its charge depend on whether the **Mortgage Loan File** is clear to close, and on the file's closing record in **Closing and Funding**.

**Counting rule.**

- When the loan file is clear to close and a closing is scheduled on it (closing status scheduled or docs out), the days counted are the calendar days from the lock's current expiration date to that closing's estimated funding date, never more than the extension days.
- When the loan file is clear to close and no closing is scheduled, the days counted are the calendar days from the current expiration date to the file's estimated closing date, never more than the extension days.
- Otherwise the days counted are the extension days in full.

For a loan file that is clear to close, and only on an extension this policy books, Larkspur also bears every day of the new extension beyond the days counted to the file's funding or closing date under the counting rule. This sits beside the two base cases in which Larkspur bears extension days: the complimentary days of a lock's first extension, and the appraisal-delay days. Those two cases still govern every other situation, apart from the relief a decided extension-charge dispute grants and the goodwill Larkspur adds when it waives an appraisal-covered charge on its own initiative.

The charged days are then the days counted less the Larkspur-borne days, never below zero. The Larkspur-borne days booked on the entry are the extension days less the charged days.

For every extension this policy books, the cost points are its charged days, counted under the counting rule, times its per-day cost after every adjustment, divided by 100 and rounded to three decimal places. Its cost is the cost points times the loan amount at lock divided by 100, rounded to the cent.

| Loan file status | Closing status | Days counted |
|---|---|---|
| Clear to close | Scheduled or docs out | Days from the current expiration date to the estimated funding date, at most the extension days |
| Clear to close | No closing scheduled | Days from the current expiration date to the estimated closing date, at most the extension days |
| Any other status | Any | The extension days in full |

### Hypothetical cases

- A clear-to-close file has a closing reading docs out, funding 4 days after the current expiration date. A 10-day extension with no other Larkspur-borne days counts 4 days. 4 days are charged, and 6 are booked as Larkspur-borne.
- The same file still in underwriting counts all 10 days.
- A clear-to-close file with no closing scheduled and an estimated closing date 12 days after the current expiration date counts at most the 10 extension days, so it counts 10.
